production.note: US model years 2003-2006. Start: Chrysler Group release of 17 July 2002, 'Pricing and Specs Announced for 2003 Dodge Viper SRT-10'. End: KBB lists 2006 'SRT10 Convertible 2D' and 'SRT10 Coupe 2D' (kbb-viper-2006); Edmunds 2008: 'After a one-year hiatus, the Dodge Viper returns for 2008' with 'an 8.4-liter V10' (edmunds-viper-2008-review), so there was no 2007 model year.

body.note: 2006 trims 'SRT10 Convertible 2D' and 'SRT10 Coupe 2D'. 2003-2005: convertible only (the release calls it a 'true convertible model'); the coupe was added for 2006 ('The all-new 2006 Dodge Viper SRT10 Coupe will be available in Dodge dealerships in the fall of 2005', supercars-viper-coupe-2006).

displacementL.note: '8.3-Liter [505 Cubic-inches]'; the Chrysler release: '505 cu. in. V-10' (chrysler-viper-srt10-2002-release). 8,275 cc per Supercars.net's table ('8275 cc / 505.0 in³', supercars-viper-srt10-2003, an enthusiast source); no manufacturer page with the cc figure was opened.

transmission.note: 'Transmission Options: M/T 6-Speed M/T'; Edmunds 2003: '6-speed manual' (edmunds-viper-2003). Tremec T56 per Supercars.net.

powerHp.note: Quote (Chrysler Group release, 17 July 2002, 2003 Viper SRT-10): "The 500 horsepower, 525 lb.-ft of torque, 505 cu. in. V-10 super car will carry a Manufacturers Suggested Retail Price (MSRP) of $79,995 (plus $800 destination) when it begins arriving in dealerships around the first of October, 2002." KBB 2003: "500 @ 5200 RPM" (kbb-viper-2003); Cars.com 2003: "500 @ 5600" (cars-com-viper-2003); KBB 2006: "500 @ 5600 RPM" (kbb-viper-2006). Edmunds' 2008 review refers to 'the former 510-horsepower V10' (edmunds-viper-2008-review); no other source gives 510 hp for 2003-2006.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (databases). 2003 convertible (the only body for 2003), 6-speed manual. Quote (KBB 2003 Viper SRT10 Roadster 2D): "Curb Weight: 3,357 pounds". Cars.com 2003 '2dr SRT-10 Convertible': "Base Curb Weight: 3,357 lbs" (cars-com-viper-2003). Edmunds 2003 'SRT-10 2dr Roadster': "3,380 lbs." (edmunds-viper-2003), and KBB 2006 convertible "3,380 pounds" (kbb-viper-2006), 0.7% higher; see discrepancies. Chrysler's release says only 'approximately 100 pounds less than previous models'. The 2006 coupe: '1565 kg / 3450 lbs' (Supercars.net, supercars-viper-coupe-2006, unattributed).

sources.publisher: Chrysler Group (release reproduced by The Auto Channel)
sources.title: Pricing and Specs Announced for 2003 Dodge Viper SRT-10-to Hit Dodge Showrooms in October

discrepancies.reason: KBB and Cars.com give 3,357 lb for the 2003 convertible; Edmunds (2003) and KBB (2006) give 3,380 lb, 0.7% higher. No source explains the difference; it may be a later revised figure.
discrepancies.resolution: 3,357 lb used: two databases agree for the reference year; the spread is within 2%.

provisionalNote: Weight (3,357 lb) rests on databases (KBB and Cars.com agree; Edmunds and KBB 2006 give 3,380 lb). A Chrysler/Dodge spec sheet or a major magazine spec panel for the 2003 Viper SRT-10 would replace it. Power (500 hp) is from Chrysler's release.
